comment: Lifecycle cases: a sequence of events applied to one zone with one active profile, and the trip state after each. startup carries the durable state the consumer finds on disk. Every event names the state expected afterwards; an event that executes an outcome names it, and an event that is refused names the refusal. Readings here are credible unless a case says otherwise.
fixtures_comment: Ratified fixture profiles that exist only in this file. Every shipped profile is a candidate and cannot be activated, so the cases run against these; they carry the shipped numbers so a consumer's evaluator is exercised at the values it will meet.

cases.name: arm_trip_latch_restart_reset
cases.note: The reference sequence: a clean start arms, a hazard trips and latches, a restart does not close the circuit, a reset is refused while the hazard persists and succeeds once it clears.

cases.name: arm_requires_safety_path
cases.note: A credible reading alone does not arm. The safety path must be confirmed first, because arming closes the circuit the runtime must then be able to open.

cases.name: arm_refused_while_tripped
cases.note: A hazard reading trips the zone before it was ever armed. Arming from tripped is not a transition: only a reset leaves tripped, so a reading that satisfies the condition can never be the most recent credible reading of a zone that is merely inactive.

cases.name: trip_from_inactive_executes_the_outcome
cases.note: A zone whose de-energised terminal state is closed carries load while inactive. A hazard reading before arming still commands the outcome; inactive means unarmed, not unprotected.

cases.name: crash_before_trip_record_is_recovered_by_the_arming_rule
cases.note: The residual crash path: the trip-intent append failed before the process died between command and record, so the restart finds neither a durable trip nor an unresolved intent. Recovery is the arming rule; the intent-recorded path is its own case.

cases.name: restart_from_armed_returns_to_inactive
cases.note: Armed is not durable across a restart. The safety path has to be confirmed again before the circuit is closed.

cases.name: reset_refused_when_not_tripped
cases.note: Reset is a transition out of tripped and nothing else.

cases.name: reset_requires_a_credible_reading
cases.note: After a restart into tripped, no reading has been seen. A reset cannot know whether the hazard cleared and is refused.

cases.name: rejected_input_does_not_move_the_state
cases.note: A rejected reading is alerted and otherwise inert: it neither trips nor counts as the credible reading arming and reset require.

cases.name: no_external_input_moves_the_state
cases.note: Once tripped, a remote command, a skill, a configuration value, a policy document and a binding revision each attempt to clear the trip. None has authority.

cases.name: external_input_cannot_arm_either
cases.note: The same sources against an inactive zone. Arming is a runtime decision made from the safety path and a credible reading, not something a document or command performs.

cases.name: intent_recorded_crash_loads_tripped
cases.note: The intent path: the append succeeded, the command was issued, and the process died before the full record committed. The restart finds no durable trip but an unresolved intent, loads the pair tripped with command_pending, and the reading-independent retry resolves the command.

cases.name: closed_terminal_startup_defers_until_non_hazard_reading
cases.note: De-energising this zone closes the protected circuit, so startup commands nothing; the first credible reading that trips no profile licenses the closing command.

cases.name: closed_terminal_startup_hazard_first_reading_never_closes
cases.note: The first credible reading satisfies the condition: the zone trips and the deferred closing command is never given — not at the trip, and not for a later clear reading, because a latched zone's circuit is closed only by reset.

cases.name: two_profiles_one_zone_defer_until_all_evaluated
cases.note: Two active profiles on one closed-terminal zone. A reading between the trip points trips one pair and not the other, and the zonal closing command is withheld because the reading did not clear every profile. A later clear reading does not revive the zonal command either: one pair is latched, and only reset closes it.

cases.name: driver_refusal_retries_without_a_reading_and_acceptance_ends_retries
cases.note: The driver refuses the trip command; the registry-owned loop retries with no further sensor reading, and once the driver accepts, a later tick does not re-issue the accepted command merely because its physical effect is unverified.

cases.name: reset_cancels_a_scheduled_retry
cases.note: A reset licenses closing the circuit; a retry scheduled before it must not fire afterwards and reopen what the operator closed.

cases.name: orphaned_trip_retires_only_through_the_local_procedure
cases.note: Retirement before orphaning is refused; after the zone leaves the binding the pair stays latched and health-visible, and the local retirement moves it to the terminal audit disposition without commanding any coil.

cases.name: legacy_tripped_record_without_status_retries
cases.note: A durable tripped record predating the command-status vocabulary proves no acceptance: it loads command_pending — the retryable status, never the one that stops retries — and the reading-independent loop resolves it.

cases.name: accepted_command_with_failed_record_recovers_persistence_only
cases.note: The driver accepted the open command but the full record write failed. Acceptance stops the outcome retries and stops nothing about persistence: the record recovery continues on its own, and never re-issues the accepted physical command.

cases.name: record_resolves_only_older_intents
cases.note: A crash between the record commit and the intent resolution leaves the older intent unresolved in the journal; the record resolves it at load, so the pair carries the record's status rather than degrading to command_pending.

cases.name: duplicate_intents_collapse_by_append_order
cases.note: Two unresolved intents for the pair; the later append governs. Its binding matches the binding in force, so the pair is not orphaned and the retry actuates — a collapse to the earlier intent would orphan the pair and skip it.

cases.name: intent_binding_mismatch_orphans_not_actuates
cases.note: The unresolved intent was commanded under a binding no longer in force. The pair loads tripped and orphaned: latched, health-visible, and never actuated through a binding it was not commanded under — the retry is skipped, and the exit is the local retirement.

cases.name: malformed_intent_entry_fails_closed
cases.note: An intent entry missing required fields, still identifiable by its position in this pair's journal: it loads the pair tripped with a pending command rather than being skipped.

cases.name: reset_clear_is_durable_and_resolves_older_intents
cases.note: A successful reset durably clears the trip record; a restart whose journal ends in that clear loads inactive, with the cleared trip's intent resolved by it rather than resurrecting the latch.

cases.name: intent_after_record_governs
cases.note: A record, then a newer unresolved intent: append order governs, so the pair loads command_pending from the intent rather than the record's acceptance — a record resolves every intent before it and none after.

cases.name: intent_after_clear_governs
cases.note: Record, reset clear, then a newer unresolved intent: the second trip's crash is not hidden by the first trip's resolution.

cases.name: acceptance_never_implies_effect
cases.note: The driver accepted the command; the effect axis stays unknown until something actually verifies it, and neither matched nor mismatched moves the latch.

cases.name: intent_wrong_zone_fails_closed
cases.note: A pair field naming another zone is a malformed entry.

cases.name: intent_wrong_profile_fails_closed
cases.note: A pair field naming another profile is a malformed entry.

cases.name: intent_empty_attempt_id_fails_closed
cases.note: attempt_id must be a non-empty string.

cases.name: intent_boolean_binding_seq_fails_closed
cases.note: binding_seq must be a positive integer, and a boolean is not one.

cases.name: intent_wrong_outcome_fails_closed
cases.note: close_protected_circuit is never an intent outcome.

cases.name: intent_string_created_at_fails_closed
cases.note: created_at_ms must be a positive integer.

cases.name: intent_string_resolved_fails_closed
cases.note: resolved must be a boolean; the string false is truthy in some languages and silently resolves the intent.

cases.name: intent_empty_zone_id_fails_closed
cases.note: The pair fields are non-empty before they are equal: an empty zone_id matching an empty enclosing zone_id is still a malformed entry. The intent's binding_seq deliberately mismatches the binding in force so the two readings diverge observably: the malformed path fails closed without an orphan mark, while a checker that let equality launder emptiness would read a well-formed intent and orphan the pair.

cases.name: justified_resolution_loads_from_the_record
cases.note: A resolved intent followed by the record that resolved it is the legitimate shape: the record's status governs and the mark is witnessed.

durable_reject_cases.name: unknown_durable_state_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: trippped is a record this machine never wrote.

durable_reject_cases.name: unreadable_intent_journal_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: Unidentifiable corruption: the journal cannot be read at all, and hardened startup refuses rather than guessing.

durable_reject_cases.name: unknown_durable_command_status_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: executed is the overclaim this contract removed; a record carrying it is a record from a vocabulary this version never wrote.

durable_reject_cases.name: tripped_without_any_record_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: durable_state tripped with neither a journal record nor a legacy record is a state the persistence rules cannot produce.

durable_reject_cases.name: duplicate_attempt_id_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: Two unresolved entries claiming one attempt identity violate nothing but the duplicate rule, so only that rule can refuse them — corruption beyond the entry level, refusing the journal.

durable_reject_cases.name: resolved_intent_without_record_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: A resolved mark with no later record or clear claims a resolution nothing durable performed. On a closed-terminal zone, loading this as inactive would eventually command the circuit closed on the strength of an unwitnessed claim.

durable_reject_cases.name: resolved_intent_without_record_refuses_even_tripped
durable_reject_cases.note: The same unwitnessed resolution with durable_state tripped: the refusal is about the journal's own coherence, not the state beside it.

durable_reject_cases.name: journal_record_without_status_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: A journal record entry with no command status. Legacy treatment is the pre-journal source's alone; a current-format row missing its status is corruption, and loading it as retryable legacy would launder it into history.

durable_reject_cases.name: journal_record_empty_status_refuses
durable_reject_cases.note: The same with an empty string, which a truthiness fallback would silently replace.
